purpose: Read-only audit of every pending XLSX feature-inventory row against the finalized native Microsoft Excel corpus. This file classifies the remaining work without changing coverage.json, source code, or shared corpus metadata.

classification_rules.operation_only: The closed native corpus already records a bounded saved package/UI specimen for the row or a clearly named sub-scope; the remaining assertion is library CRUD, projection, validation, recalculation, refresh, runtime, or another operation beyond this file-only native audit.
classification_rules.observed_native_ui_limitation: The residual audit or the inspected native session provides a bounded reason that the current native producer has no usable local authoring route. This never converts package absence into format-level unsupported status.
classification_rules.external_handoff: Authoring requires a certificate/identity, password handoff, online provider/account, add-in manifest/service, or another external producer. A local native workbook alone is insufficient for an authoritative fixture.
classification_rules.genuinely_missing_authorable_family: A distinct saved family is authorable in native Excel and has no exact finalized fixture. A concrete small target is listed; the target is not a duplicate of an existing operation or storage fixture.

scope.evidence_policy: Native package facts are cited only at the scope recorded in the referenced inspection JSON. No rendering, recalculation, refresh, external execution, control execution, chart semantic parity, or broad XLSB/XLS parity is inferred. A missing part in one inspected package is recorded as fixture scope, never as proof that Excel cannot produce it.

concrete_missing_authorable_targets.target: Enter two 2x2 source blocks on separate sheets, use Data > Consolidate with Sum into a third sheet, and save a marker beside the result; inspect consolidation source references and cached result cells.
concrete_missing_authorable_targets.reason: No finalized native XLSX contains consolidation metadata. The target exercises a native Excel operation absent from the table, pivot, or formula-owner fixtures; the audit must keep calculation semantics separate from stored metadata.

concrete_missing_authorable_targets.target: On a fresh workbook, use the observed Tools > Track Changes > Highlight Changes route, enable the available legacy tracking mode, make two deterministic cell edits, save, and inspect revision users/headers/log relationships; attempt Accept or Reject only as a separate saved-state observation.
concrete_missing_authorable_targets.reason: The current Excel session exposed both Track Changes commands, disabled until tracking is enabled. No finalized XLSX contains revision metadata, so this is a concrete native target rather than another ordinary cell-edit fixture.
